en: Salutations to that Blessed One, the Great Soul Caitanya, who destroys the impurities of the Kali age and delivers beings from the ocean of worldly existence. 1.
That which was revealed by Brahmā Haridāsa to Śrī Rūpa, I shall relate it all; listen with full attention. 2.
Upon hearing this, all the Vaiṣṇavas were delighted and overwhelmed with love; they questioned him respectfully with voices faltering with affection. (3)
Indeed, out of compassion for the Vaiṣṇavas, having then remembered the words of my father, I shall describe the names of the Lord's forms at the end of the eon. 4.
Meditation:

Oṃ. Of this *Sahasranāmastotra* of Śrī Kṛṣṇacaitanya, Nārāyaṇa is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (*chanda*), and the worshipful devotion to the Blessed Lord (*śrīmad-bhagavad-bhakti*) is the deity (*devatā*). For the pleasure of Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, it is employed (*viniyoga*) in the path of the thousand names of Śrī Kṛṣṇacaitanya.

Oṃ, obeisance to the one who is the embodiment of the accumulation of love, the beloved of the gopīs, the Great Soul. Oṃ, the sustainer of the universe, eternally blissful, the conqueror of the world, the creator of the universe, possessed of great majesty, the soul of all, the fair-limbed one, and the source of all that is fair. (5)
He is golden-hued, long-armed, long-necked, pure, and the possessor of wealth; he is consciousness, the conscious one, the mind, the very form of the intellect, and the Lord himself.

He was the very limb of Rādhā, possessed of the nature of Rādhikā, ever seeking Rādhā, and sweet-spoken; he was a knower of ethics, a knower of all dharmas, full of devotion, and the Supreme Person. ||7||
He is the possessor of spiritual power, possessed of great fortitude, a knower of the scriptures, eternally new, majestic, the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, whose very form is aesthetic rasa. ||8||
He is without beginning or end, the sustainer, the ornament of the earth, and pure; he possesses excellent limbs, is agile, skillful, majestic, and associated with the virtuous. ||9||
He is the intoxicated one, the madman, the hero, the leader of the steadfast, and the lover of aesthetic flavor; he wears red garments, bears the staff, is a renunciant, and is adorned as an ascetic.
Bearing a staff, holding a parasol, with a discus in hand, compassionate, all-seeing, unarmed, the teacher of all, he is the destroyer of the defects of the Kali age. ||11||
The venerable Guru is an ocean of mercy, valorous, and Janārdana; he is the seizer of barbarians, the destroyer of evil conduct, the remover of the wicked, and one filled with compassion.
A celibate student, the best of ascetics, devoted to Brahman, a Brāhmaṇa, and wise; the king of the twice-born, a universal emperor, a seer, and compassionate toward the wretched. ||13||
Free from desire, a purifier who knows the true goal, smokeless and like a fire, he is not to be praised by men; having the form of Hara, he will become a leader of men. ||14||
Vṛkodara is a hero in generosity, a hero in battle, and a hero in compassion; he is a hero in wisdom, a great hero, a hero in tranquility, and one of majestic power. ||15||
The illustrious Jiṣṇu, the victorious one who wanders, the patient one of beautiful appearance, the most excellent Nara, difficult to behold, the moon of Navadvīpa. ||16||
Candrahāsya, Candranakha, Balimadudara, Bali, Sūryaprabha, Sūryāṃśu, Sūryāṅga, and Maṇibhūṣaṇa. ||17||

With a neck like a conch-shell, the beauty of his cheeks, a deep navel, and beautiful eyes, this Brahmin—the son of the Lord of the World—possessed limbs of jewels and was adorned with jewel-ornaments. (18)

Seeking the sacred ford, the giver of the sacred ford, the sacred ford itself, the limb of the sacred ford, the achiever of the sacred ford, the abode of the sacred ford, dwelling in the sacred ford, the servant of the sacred ford, and yet without any external support. ||19||
Tīrthālādi, Tīrthaprada, Brāhmaka, the wanderer of Brahmā, Śrīvāsapaṇḍitānanda, and the one who brings joy to Rāmānanda. ||20||
The beloved servant of Gadādhara, the valiant one, the beloved of Śaṅkara; the yogi, the bestower of yoga, yoga itself, the performer of yoga, and the creator of the threefold yoga. ||21||

He is the all-encompassing, the giver of all things, the Infinite, whose every limb is complete, and from whom all things originate; he is the archer, whose weapon is the arrow, the eloquent speaker, the Lord of Speech, and he who is not born from a womb.

He is intelligence, truth, strength, splendor, and steadfastness; he is the form of all moving beings, the enemy of Mura, the nourisher, the creator, the man-lion, and the increaser of humanity. ||23||

He is beyond action yet the giver of action, the Lord who knows action and the destroyer of action; He is priceless, the agent, the action itself, worthy of ritual performance, and the subduer of karma. ||24||

He is devoid of qualities yet possessed of all qualities; the Lord, the Ordainer, the singer of the Sāman hymns, the unconquered; he who has conquered his breath, conquered his vital force, conquered the bodiless god of love, and conquered his senses. ||25||

He whose nature is Kṛṣṇa, whose name is Kṛṣṇa, whose self is Kṛṣṇa, whose leader is Kṛṣṇa; he who is non-dual, yet possesses duality as his companion, who has a twofold state, the protector, and the self-controlled one. ||26||
Śrīvāsa, Śrīdharāhvaya, Halanāyakasāravid, Viśvarūpānuja, Candra, Varīyān, Mādhava, and Acyuta. (27)

Attached to form, he is of virtuous conduct, a knower of qualities, and one who manifests many states; he is devoid of qualities, transcendent of qualities, a grasper of qualities, and an ocean of qualities. ||28||

He is the bliss of Brahman, eternal bliss, the bliss of love, and the supreme delighter; he is the remover of the censurable, the avoider of the censurable, the destroyer of the censurable, and the one who grants complete satisfaction. ||29||

Yajñabāhu was self-disciplined and did not perform sacrifices for show; he was the best among those who have conquered the Kali age, possessed pure luster, was free from worldly attachments, and was like a purifying fire.

Hiraṇyagarbha, the subtle self, the sovereign Vairāja, the lord of the passionless; the playful one, the majestic one, the possessor of his own portions, the one in the supreme state, the crest-jewel. ||31||

The destroyer of illusion, the master of illusion, the possessor of illusion, the proponent of illusion, the discerning one; the concealer of Kṛṣṇa, the speaker of Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of sense objects, the formless one. ||32||

He is free from conceptual construction, the Lord of Māyā, the one who enters Māyā, the beloved of Vraja, the sovereign of Vraja, the lord of Vraja, and the delighter of the cowherds and the herds of cattle. ||33||

He is a resident of Vraja, his very nature is Vraja, and he is the most excellent leader of Vraja; he is fond of secrecy, his disposition is secret, he is the desired one, and he is the refuge of the noble lineage. ||34||
Following passion, an ocean of passion, whose very self is passion, the increaser of passion; arisen from passion, the witness of love, Bhaṭṭanātha, the eternal one. ||35||
Gopālabhaṭṭaga is pleased, beloved by Lokanātha, and skillful; he is two-armed, six-armed, and embodied, the destroyer of the pride of kings. ||36||
He who is beloved by Kāśimiśra, the venerable one worthy of homage, the son of Śacī; the lord of Miśra and Purandara, the beloved of Raghunātha, the impetuous one. ||37||
He who strips away the pride of universal monarchs, the unfailing enemy, the beloved of wealth; he who is innate, the lord of the innate, the eternal, and one who is distressed by love. ||38||
Afflicted by the absence of joy, with pale cheeks and distressed by grief, he is a talker who speaks much; though pure and straightforward, his gait is crooked—such is Śiva. (39)
The lotus-eyed one, who manifests the variety of love, is struck with emotion; he is full of pride for his beloved, clever, devoted to his beloved, and intent upon his beloved. (40)
With hair standing on end, trembling, with tearful face, he is the destroyer of sorrow; fond of laughter, a maker of laughter, joined with laughter, and a connoisseur of laughter. ||41||

He is a village buffoon, a creator of laughter, characterized by the triple-bend posture, and agitated by dancing; his body hair stands erect, his hands are raised, he utters loud cries, and he is full of emotional transformations.
He who delights in existence, the steadfast and peaceful one, the courageous-limbed, the hero of the wise; the abode of the gods, the dwelling of the gods, the god of gods, the mind-born one. ||43||
Hemādri possesses the golden luster of gold; Sumeru is the abode of Brahmā; Airāvata has the brilliance of gold; Śaraghna is the bestower of all desires. ||44||
With thighs like those of a young elephant, long eyes, and trembling eyebrows, eyes, and nose; he is the knot of names, the enumeration of names, bound by existence, and the remover of thirst. 45.

The attractor of evil, the remover of evil, the destroyer of evil, the purifier of evil; the destroyer of pride, the giver of wealth, the slayer of enemies, the destroyer of arrogance, the slayer of foes, the Sweet One (Madhu). ||46||

He is the destroyer of form, the destroyer of dress, divine, the kinsman of the distressed, and composed of compassion; he is the one whose syllables are nectar, who tastes nectar, whose nature is nectar, and the most desirable one. ||47||

He is liberated, the giver of liberation, the one who is free, known as the liberated, and the remover of obstacles to liberation; he is free from doubt, devoid of ego, free from enmity, and the dispeller of calamities. ||48||

He is the wise one of fresh splendor, the lord of the twice-born of the nine islands; he is unrestrained, worshipped by the gods, the preceptor of the gods, and the slayer of the enemies of the gods. 49.
The best of gods, the remover of reproach, the destroyer of debate, the one who brings satisfaction; the well-illuminated, the long-armed, the knower of friends, and the ornament of poets. ||50||

Bestower of boons, with the side-glance of a boon, possessing a pair of boons, the leader of boons; he whose smile is like a flower, who has the fragrance of a lotus, who is as red as a ruby, and who is ever awake. ||51||

Ascending, walking upon the true path, the giver of life, the singer of the upward song; beloved by the people, the delight of the people, the progenitor of sages, and the object of the people's longing. ||52||

Unborn, the abode of birth, the delighter of people, whose mind is moist with compassion for beings; the Lord of the world, the kinsman of the world, the God of the world, the Master of the world. ||53||

He brings about the birth [of beings], he is the delight of people, and he possesses an intense joy for his progenitors; he is fond of strife, he is praised even in the Kali age, and he increases the pride of those in the Kali age. ||54||

The dispeller of the Kali age, eternal bliss, the creator of the Kali age, the one honored by the Kali age; the one who causes prosperity, the upholder of the Vedas, the increaser, and the bestower of growth. ||55||

The refuge of prosperity, the skillful one, whose limbs are compassion, the protector from the Kali age, the one blessed by the Kali age, the knower of the right time, and the illuminator of merit in the Kali age. ||56||
Free from anxiety, noble and playful, firm in speech, beloved by his lover; he touches the left side, possesses a leftward disposition, has a leftward form, and is captivating. (57)

Beyond the senses, the presiding lord of the gods, the overseer of the world, one who has accomplished all that was to be done; the creator of the beginning of the ages, the maker of the ages, the knower of the ages, and the leader of the ages. ||58||
The revolution of the ages, the limit of the ages, possessing time, the wielder of the power of time; affection, eternal, joyful, the conqueror of the universe, and the deluder of the intellect.

He is the twilight, the performer of meditation, the meditator, and the one who possesses the auspicious union of meditation; he is the renowned self, established in the heart, and the grasper of the village-restrainer.

He who is the source of musical notes, who delights in the melodic scales, whose form is adorned by the notes themselves; he who perceives the song, who is fond of singing, the singer, and the one who causes the song to flourish. ||61||

He is indeed worthy of song, immeasurable, the one who honors others, the sustainer of the universe, and the victorious; he has the form of the churned ocean of milk and the shape of a fish containing love within its womb. ||62||

Bibhatsu, whose heart is filled with aesthetic emotion (bhāva), invisible yet revealing the sacrificial grass (barhis); restrained by wisdom, firm-minded, dear to the Self of all, and highly intelligent. ||63||
Immeasurable, the light of all-knowing, tawny, many-headed, radiant, of vast fame, exceedingly long, of bull-like deeds, and bull-like form.
Veda was the upholder of the Śruti and Smṛti; Śrutijña was the subverter of the Śruti; Hṛdispṛśa was the Ātman; and Vicakṣaṇa was the essence of the Śruti. ||65||
He is a peacock, devoid of compassion; he is a disseminator of medical science, an adversary of the Mīmāṃsakas, the source of the Vedāṅgas and the meaning of the Vedas, and the ultimate goal. ||66||

He who knows the high and the low, who is difficult to overcome, whose limbs are free from passion, and who is the refuge of the virtuous; he who is innumerable, whose nature is immeasurable, who bestows perfection, and who is the means for attaining perfection. ||67||
He is the bridge of dharma, devoted to dharma, whose very self is dharma, and who cultivates dharma; he is the cutter of rising doubts, the manifestation of power, eternal, and steadfast.
Pure in soul, with beautiful longing, indefinable, and fond of spiritual practice; devoted to sacred texts, consisting of sacred texts, the source of the scriptures, and magnanimous. (69)

He is beyond caste, yet the abode of all castes; he is not bound to a stage of life, yet possesses the four stages of life. He is not a Brahmin, yet the creator of Brahmins; he is worthy of praise, yet the destroyer of kingdoms.

He is the one who brings the uncontrolled under control, who is intent upon the service of Śrī, whose speed is like that of the mind, who fulfills all desires, and who is the embodiment of pure devotion and fame. ||71||

The possessor of treasures, the treasure of devotion, difficult to attain, the creator of the state beyond difficulty; the one who cuts away [sins], the peerless fame, the immortal, the beloved of Muraja (the drum). ||72||

The fifth state is Śṛṅgāra (the erotic), which is the source of all states and follows immediately after them; it is conquered by devotion, feasts upon love, and promotes the ninefold manifestation of devotion. ||73||

He who possesses the triple strength of Trigarta, whose delight is threefold, who fulfills the three desires, who increases affection, who is the restrainer, who has transcended weariness, who nourishes, and who is free from all feverish distress. ||74||

The fever of love is worthy of celestial chariots; it is the destroyer of wealth and the dispeller of dreams. It is the means of deliverance, meritorious by name alone, and yet devoid of both sin and merit. ||75||

He who removes offenses, he who is to be protected, the giver of well-being, whose ornament is well-being; he whose self is pure, who goes to the pure, who is pure, whose nature is purity, and who possesses a great sound.

The knower of the field, the conqueror of the field, dwelling within the field, the progenitor of the world; the destroyer of fear, the giver of fear, the radiant one, endowed with the state of being secondary. ||77||
Adorned, the creator of the mandala, possessing the Vaijayantī garland and the sacred thread; with variegated limbs, painted, and wonderful, he reveals the hearts of his devotees. ||78||

The goal of wisdom, the giver of wisdom, wisdom itself, the upholder of wisdom, the increaser of wisdom; the upholder of the mountain of love, the bearer of love, the carrier of delight, and the touch of delight. ||79||

He whose eye is love, who is dense with love, whose heart is love, and who fulfills love; he who moves in the profound, whose dwelling is outside, who moves according to the performance of inner feeling—he is the Lord.

He is not of manifold form, not of manifold existence, not of manifold self, nor does he assume manifold forms; his joints are relaxed, his qualities are exhausted, he has cast off all evil, and his fame is vast.
Wide-striding, wide-necked, of vast being, and wide-paced; he whose nature is shaken free from stain, who is effortless and beyond favor.
The fire is smokeless, well-blazing, intensely hot, and the consumer of oblations; it is one, pervading the great elements, yet existing as many distinct entities.
A decisive ruler who acts without being prompted, one who turns back wicked villages, a kinsman to the Brahmins, beloved, pleasing, and one whose limbs inspire delight—such is the lord of men. (84)
The overseer of the world, golden-hued, possessing a golden lotus, the crest-jewel; the golden pitcher, the bridge of dharma, the lord of the world, the teacher of the universe. ||85||

Named Lohitākṣa, he is established in action and abides in the cave of the heart; his life-force is the vital essence, he is supreme in delight, and he is the ocean of rasa, agitated by his own passion.

The ocean of existence, the cloud of devotion raining down aesthetic flavor, crowded with people; he who holds a yellow lotus, who has a blue and yellow luster, the enjoyer of pleasure, the elixir of life. ||87||
The unmanifested one, the golden lotus, the colorless one, the vision of the virtuous; the deathless one, the giver of death, the unobstructed, the unifier, and the deceiver of death. ||88||

He is the one intoxicated by love, the dancer of kīrtana, the divine father of congregational chanting; he is the multitude of devotion, the one whose purpose is perfectly accomplished, the bestower of perfection, and the means for attaining perfection.
He whose belly is love, whose arms are love, the sustainer of the world, the lord of the quarters; he who is dark within and fair without, the beholder, the expansion of delight.

He who fulfills all intentions, whose nature is desire, the incomparable sustainer of bodies, whose purpose is prosperity, whose side-glances are compassion, the creator of rivers, and the one who is affectionate toward his devotees. ||91||
Free from envy, supreme bliss, clad in a loincloth, nourisher of devotion, free from deceit, wearing a garland of names, swift, and possessing all auspicious marks. ||92||
Moderate in diet, with steady gaze, established in resolve, abiding in joy, dwelling in the forest of delight, subsequently contented, and filled with tranquility. ||93||
The agitator, the heroic one, the path, the upholder of the path, the showman of the way; he who dwells in the lowest stage, the humble-minded, the expansion, the imperishable seed. ||94||

The embodiment of delusion, subtle in movement, the great sacrificer, the increaser of sacrificial sessions; the one with a beautiful face, the inducer of sleep, the beginningless, the doer of good, and the destroyer of sin. ||95||
Śrīnivāsa, the profound-souled one, honored by Śṛṅgāra and Kanaka; he is the deep and impenetrable Creator, possessed of the limbs and sub-limbs [of the Vedas], and the lover of Dharma.

One whose passion has arisen, one who possesses variety, one who brings glory, one worthy of praise; one whose limbs are moistened by tears from the eyes, one filled [with longing], and one who fulfills delight. ||97||

He who is the path of praise, the presiding lord of hymns, the one worthy of praise, and the one filled with praise; he whose seed is drawn up, the dwelling place of peace, the embodiment of love, and the one possessing a hundred fires. ||98||

A kinsman to his devotees, a friend to the world, a kinsman through love, and one who subdued hundreds; possessing the intellect of truth, a retainer of sacred revelation, and the best among all wielders of weapons. ||99||
He is the gateway to devotion, the abode of devotion, the temple of love, and the destroyer of worldly obstruction; he is intensely agitated, his mind reeling, and his body trembling. ||100||

He is the dispeller of doubts born from wandering through worldly existence, a mass of love that removes all sorrow; he is the teacher of compassion, the embodiment of attachment to love, the divine wisdom, and eternally youthful. 101.
He who goes to the ocean, who is embraced by love, who is subject to love, who is discerning, who resembles the filaments of a lotus, who bestows love, and who is the restrainer. 102.
He is dispassionate, free from enmity, indifferent, and not subject to the influence of Nārada; he stands in a humble posture, is skillful, emaciated, and deceives those who live as rogues. ||103||
The one who causes the name to proceed is Anartha; the Dharma is the personage such as the Guru and others; Nyagrodha is Janaka; and Vainateya is the tree of devotion. 104.
Absorbed in love, deluded regarding his own self, and following the nature of the self, he is the Virāṭ; delighting in his own sweetness, he is known as Gaura, assuming the form of a brāhmaṇa. (105)

He is the embodiment of Rādhā, possessed of great ecstatic love (mahābhāva), the one to be attained, and ever intent on worship; he is the soul of the mistress of the gopīs, invisible, and the fulfiller of his own divine office. ||106||

He has an eternal abode, an eternal form, and is the illuminator of eternal existence; he is established in a stable state, yet possesses a restless intellect, moves with clarity, and nourishes devotion. ||107||
He is omnipresent, the bridge to the shore [of liberation], seated in the heart, the lotus-seated one; he is the Lord who follows all states of being and the performer of all auspiciousness. 108.
Thus has been told this eternal, beautiful collection of a thousand names of Viṣṇu, the dweller in Goloka, who possesses a fair form and carries the Śārṅga bow. (109)
This [work] called the Gaurasahasra destroys disease, removes sorrow, bestows love and devotion upon men, and is the supreme attractor of Govinda. (110)
He who, being self-restrained, recites with devotion at dawn, at midday, at twilight, and at midnight, attains delight in Caitanya.
He in whose mind the deity Gaurī exists as his very self will certainly abandon all sense objects and become one whose bliss consists of pure being. 112.
It must not be given to just anyone, for otherwise devotion to the gift would diminish; it should be given to one who is humble, tranquil, devoted to the Guru, and wise. (113)
"To him it should be given, and from him it should be received"—this indeed is the teaching of Viṣṇu.
Thus ends the *Sahasranāmastotra* of Śrī Kṛṣṇacaitanyacandra, composed by the illustrious poet Karṇapūra.
The Morning Recollection Hymn to the Supreme Brahman (Parabrahma-prātaḥsmaraṇa-stotra)

At dawn, I remember that which is the reality of the Self, throbbing within the heart—existence, consciousness, and bliss; the state of the supreme *paramahaṃsa*, the fourth (*turīya*). That which eternally perceives the states of dreaming, waking, and deep sleep—that partless Brahman am I, and not a collection of elements. (1)

At dawn, I worship with my mind that which is unattainable by speech; by whose grace all words shine forth. That very one whom the Vedas describe through the words "not this, not this"—him they call the God of gods, the unborn, the infallible, and the supreme.

At dawn, I bow to Him who is beyond darkness, whose color is like the sun, the full and eternal state known as Puruṣottama; in whom this entire world, though He is of infinite form, is reflected like a serpent upon a rope. (3)
Whoever recites these three meritorious verses, which are the ornament of the three worlds, at the time of dawn, shall go to the supreme state. (4)
